title: COPY_TABLE_DEPENDENTS errors printed then ignored; FINISH without dml_lock_timeout
expected_feedback: Critical: num_errors is an OUT parameter Oracle requires the caller to check before continuing, and printing it is not checking it — the block proceeds to SYNC and FINISH whatever the value. A non-zero count means some dependent object failed to clone, so the cutover can complete with indexes, constraints, triggers or grants silently missing on a 60M-row production table; the first symptom is usually a full scan or a constraint that stopped being enforced. Raise on num_errors > 0 and query DBA_REDEFINITION_ERRORS to see which objects failed and why. Separately, FINISH_REDEF_TABLE is called without dml_lock_timeout (12.1+), leaving the final swap on the release default rather than a value chosen for the window — pass an explicit value such as 30 so the cutover neither aborts on the first concurrent DML after hours of copying nor waits forever behind a long transaction. Finally, take the dependent-object inventory before starting and diff it after FINISH: num_errors = 0 alone does not prove the interim table gained everything the original had.
violated_rule: DBMS_REDEFINITION error gates must halt the workflow
